# Design: JStack v3.5 — Azure Toolbox

**Generated by:** `/office-hours` on 2026-05-28
**Branch:** `v3-dev` (v3.5 lever på samma branch tills v3.0.0 taggat)
**Repo:** Azureflipper/jokerman-session-setup
**Status:** APPROVED — 2026-05-28 by Azureflipper
**Mode:** Startup (Intrapreneurship adaptation — MS-internal solo-champion)
**Supersedes:** none (first v3.5 design)

> Sex forcing-frågor + premise-check + 3 alternativ. Operator valde B (agent-integrated depth). Designen reflekterar det beslut.

---

## Problem Statement

Operatorn (CAIP-SE Solution Engineer) sitter med två återkommande sorter Azure-arbete som dagens verktyg inte adresserar bra:

1. **On-demand knowledge surfacing per Azure-tjänst.** Inför ett kundmöte om en specifik resurs (ExpressRoute, Front Door, APIM, Azure OpenAI, ...) behövs en strukturerad rundown — vad det är, fallgropar, ELI5 + L500-versioner, kostnad, POC-flow, kundens topp-10-frågor, latest greatest, var diagram/skisser finns. Idag stitchas detta från Microsoft Learn + bloggar + GPT + Slack-kollegor.
2. **Discovery / build / area-expert quick-skills** (deferred till v3.6+) — remote env-review (CAF/WAF), ALZ/SLZ-templates, etc.

v3 levererade 78 agents (incl. 15 ms-specific: AzureArchitect, AzureOpenAIAdvisor, BicepReviewer, GraphAPIAdvisor, M365CopilotAdvisor, ARMTemplateReviewer, KeyVaultAuditor) som idag är subagent-roller väntande på orkestrering. v3.5 är första iterationen där dessa agents får ett konkret konsumtionsmönster.

## Demand Evidence

Per D1: **Self-driven**. Operatorn är primary user. Team-adoption (MS-Sweden CAIP-SE, ~10-15 SE:s) är hypotetisk — om operatorn dogfoodar och ser värde, evangeliseras det vidare. Detta är klassiskt intrapreneurship-mönster: solo-champion proves value, then expands.

Ärlighet: utan named team-pain är vi inte i läge att marknadsföra detta som MS-CAIP-SE-suite. v3.5 är operator-extension; vidare expansion sker när dogfooding visar att shapen funkar i operatorns egen verklighet.

## Status Quo

Per D2: **KNOWLEDGE-cluster** är akut. Senaste 30 dagarnas painmoment har varit att samla strukturerad info om en specifik Azure-tjänst inför kundmöte. Aktuell workflow:
- 5-10 tabbar Microsoft Learn
- 2-3 bloggar (om operatorn minns rätt namn)
- GPT-frågor som kanske är aktuella, kanske inte
- Slack-kollegor (om det är akut)
- Egna anteckningar från tidigare engagements (om de hittas)

Tid spenderat: ofta 60-120 min för en deep-prep. Resultat: bra-nog till kundmöte men inkonsistent från service till service, och svårt att dela vidare till en kollega.

DISCOVERY (env-review) och BUILD (ALZ/SLZ) är också painpoints men inte lika frekventa — deferred.

## Target User & Narrowest Wedge

**Operator** (self), CAIP-SE arbetar Azure-engagements.

**Wedge:** Toolbox med distinkta `/az-*` "weapons" där första är `/az-tldr <service>`. Mål: operator reachar för verktyget i nästa Azure-kundprep istället för att stitcha Learn + bloggar.

**First dogfood target:** ExpressRoute (D3). Operator citerade den explicit i prompten. Klassisk networking-pain där kundföreställningar oftast är fel, väldokumenterad CAF/WAF-position, innehållsrikt på latest-greatest (Premium, Global Reach, FastPath).

## Constraints

- Self-driven, ej team-driven (per D1)
- Scaffolding-only architecture (per JStack core philosophy)
- MS-internal first; ingen public marketplace-submission av v3.5
- Reuse v3-investering (per Premise 5) — befintliga agents + `/generate-web`
- Knowledge freshness via linking, ej generation (per Premise 4)
- Compliance: 5-rules hard-gate gäller (no customer data, no secrets, MS SSO only, no prod-mutations, first-party first)
- Voice tier: `internal` för operator-facing rundowns. `trailblazer` om någon sektion delas mot kund (sällan).

## Premises (locked per D5)

1. **Toolbox pattern.** `/az-*` prefix, separata skills per "weapon". Ingen mega-skill. Varje weapon invokerbar oberoende.
2. **Första weapon = `/az-tldr <service>`.** On-demand. Andra weapon `/az-review` skjuts till v3.6+.
3. **Content depth lever i skill body** (eller per-service-fil), curated per-service med "as-of YYYY-MM-DD"-stämpel. Kvartalsvis refresh.
4. **Knowledge freshness via länkning, ej generation.** Skill pekar på Microsoft Learn + namngivna bloggar + officiella diagram. Vi curate:ar STRUKTUREN; MS curate:ar source-of-truth.
5. **Reuse v3-infrastruktur.** Befintliga ms-specific agents plockas som subagents. `/generate-web` för HTML när delningsbar rapport behövs.
6. **Validation = operator dogfoodar i verklig kundprep inom första veckan efter ship.** Operator's egen användning är success-signal.

## Cross-Model Perspective

Phase 3.5 skipped per operator energy (forward-momentum prioritet). Codex/subagent second-opinion kan kallas efter v3.5 om operator vill challenge designen retroactively.

## Approaches Considered

### Approach A: Lean MVP (per-service-files + MD only)
- Inga subagents. Pure content-presentation.
- Effort: S (~3 dagar human / ~3h CC)
- Risk: Låg
- **Trade-off:** Snabbast till dogfood men "platt" output relativt v3-investering

### Approach B: Agent-integrated (subagent-orchestration + multi-format) — SELECTED
- Subagents mappas per service-area
- Multi-format: MD + MS-brandad HTML via `/generate-web`
- Effort: M (~2v human / ~1d CC)
- Risk: Medium
- **Trade-off:** Mer arbete men ger verklig depth och visar v3-agents-värde

### Approach C: Hybrid curated + WebSearch (live-research)
- WebSearch för "latest greatest"-sektioner
- Effort: M
- Risk: Medium-Hög (bryter Premise 4)
- **Trade-off:** Stays-current men slop-risk

## Recommended Approach: B — Agent-integrated toolbox

### Architecture

```
skills/az-tldr/
├── SKILL.md                       ← orchestration logic
├── services/
│   ├── _template.md               ← template for new services
│   ├── expressroute.md            ← FIRST SHIPPED (deep content)
│   └── README.md                  ← list of supported services + status
├── sections/
│   ├── _section-template.md       ← per-section sub-template
│   └── README.md                  ← what each section means
└── agent-mapping.yaml             ← service → relevant subagents
```

### Skill flow (per invocation)

```
/az-tldr expressroute
   │
   ▼
1. SKILL.md reads services/expressroute.md (curated structure)
2. SKILL.md reads agent-mapping.yaml → spawns matched subagents
   - ExpressRoute → [AzureArchitect, KeyVaultAuditor (if private peering)]
   - Azure OpenAI → [AzureOpenAIAdvisor, RAIReviewer]
   - APIM → [GraphAPIAdvisor (if Graph-related), SecurityAuditor]
3. Each subagent gets the service-context + their assigned section
4. SKILL.md assembles: curated content + agent outputs → unified rundown
5. Default output: markdown to terminal
6. Optional flag --html → pipes assembled content to /generate-web for MS-brandad HTML
```

### Service content template (the 15 sections per operator's prompt)

Per service-fil följer denna struktur:

```yaml
---
service: ExpressRoute
short_name: er
category: networking
caf_pillars: [security, reliability, performance]
waf_pillars: [security, reliability, performance, cost, operational-excellence]
as_of: 2026-05-28
refresh_quarterly: true
subagent_mapping:
  primary: AzureArchitect
  secondary: [KeyVaultAuditor]  # if private peering or BGP-cert handling
---

# ExpressRoute — TLDR

## §1 — What it is (one paragraph)
[Curated text]

## §2 — What it does (operator-internal, no jargon)
[Curated text]

## §3 — How it's used (3-4 patterns)
[Curated patterns: site-to-Azure, BGP peering, ExpressRoute Direct, Global Reach]

## §4 — Frameworks it lives in
- CAF: <position in Cloud Adoption Framework>
- WAF: <how each pillar applies>
- Zero Trust: <reference>
- Azure landing zones: <ALZ ER connectivity sub design>

## §5 — Top 10 things to know
[10 hard truths: SKU choice, redundancy, peering types, ExpressRoute Direct vs Provider, billing model, FastPath, Global Reach, ARS vs vNet Gateway, MACsec, ER Metro]

## §6 — Known pitfalls (top 10)
[10 real pitfalls operator has seen or curated from MS field reports]

## §7 — What's required of customer
[Bandwidth, location, BGP capability, hardware requirements, customer-side router configs]

## §8 — 10 typical customer questions (real painpoints)
[Q&A pairs based on real customer pushback]

## §9 — Latest greatest (with as-of date)
[ExpressRoute Metro GA, FastPath GA scope, Global Reach pricing changes — point to MS source for each]

## §10 — Read further
- Microsoft Learn: [URLs]
- Diagrams: [URLs to Learn architectures section]
- Reference architectures: [URLs to ALZ / ER hub-spoke]
- Well-known bloggers:
  - John Savill (azurearchitectures.com / YouTube): [URL]
  - Daniel Mauser (MS): [blog URL]
  - <add named experts>

## §11 — ELI5 explanation (for non-technical customer-side decision-makers)
[Plain English]

## §12 — Level-500 explanation (for customer's senior architect)
[Deep technical: BGP attributes, MACsec, ExpressRoute FastPath internals, MSEE architecture]

## §13 — What it means for enterprise customer
[Strategic / outcomes language: cost predictability, sovereign-cloud connectivity, hybrid posture, audit-readiness]

## §14 — Commercial perspective
- Cost model: [circuit + bandwidth + egress + provider]
- Indicative pricing: [SKU ranges $/mo]
- POC viability: [yes/no/with-caveats — ExpressRoute is NOT POC-friendly per typical contracts]
- First commercial commitment threshold: [typical entry-point]

## §15 — Implementation flow (first meeting → CSA handover)
1. **First meeting (SE):** Understand customer's connectivity scenarios, current MPLS/SD-WAN, regulatory constraints
2. **Discovery (SE):** Geography, peering preference, bandwidth forecast, redundancy requirement
3. **Design proposal (SE + customer arch):** Topology sketch, SKU recommendation, redundancy strategy
4. **Pre-sales technical close (SE):** Quote validation, provider selection
5. **CSA handover:** Implementation timeline, IaC drop-in (Bicep/AVM module references), cutover plan
```

### Agent mapping spec (`agent-mapping.yaml`)

```yaml
mappings:
  ExpressRoute:
    primary: AzureArchitect
    sections:
      § 4-frameworks: AzureArchitect
      § 13-enterprise: AzureArchitect
      § 14-commercial: AzureArchitect
    secondary:
      KeyVaultAuditor: applies-when [private-peering, ipsec-overlay]

  Azure OpenAI:
    primary: AzureOpenAIAdvisor
    sections:
      § 4-frameworks: AzureOpenAIAdvisor
      § 13-enterprise: AzureOpenAIAdvisor
    secondary:
      RAIReviewer: applies-when [customer-facing-output, sensitive-use-scenario]

  APIM:
    primary: GraphAPIAdvisor    # closest match in current agent catalog
    sections:
      § 4-frameworks: GraphAPIAdvisor
    secondary:
      SecurityAuditor: applies-when [public-tier, oauth-flow]
```

### Output format

**Default:** Markdown to stdout (terminal). Operator reads in their CLI session, scrolls section-by-section.

**Optional `--html`:** Pipes assembled output to `/generate-web` which renders MS-brandad HTML using existing `scaffolding/03-ms-team/doc-gen/default-templates/default-web-template.html` (current generic fallback) eller MS brand assets om `~/.jstack/brand/` är populated.

**Optional `--md-file <path>`:** Writes assembled MD to file. Useful for sharing in Teams/Slack-chat.

## First-cut implementation plan

### v3.5 deliverables (this iteration)

1. `skills/az-tldr/SKILL.md` — orchestration body (300-400 lines)
2. `skills/az-tldr/services/_template.md` — service-content template (150 lines)
3. `skills/az-tldr/services/expressroute.md` — FIRST SHIPPED service, deep content (~800-1200 lines incl. all 15 sections)
4. `skills/az-tldr/services/README.md` — list of supported services + status table
5. `skills/az-tldr/sections/README.md` — section-glossary, what each § means + how subagents are invoked per section
6. `skills/az-tldr/agent-mapping.yaml` — service → subagent mapping (5-10 entries for likely-future services as placeholder)
7. `tests/unit/az-toolbox-service-files.sh` — verifies all services/ files validate against template + as-of dates fresh
8. `docs/per-cli/az-toolbox.md` — operator install + invocation guide
9. Add `/az-tldr` to README skill-catalog
10. CHANGELOG.md v3.5.0-dev entry

### Future weapons (v3.6+ pipeline, NOT shipped in v3.5)

Preview of what `/az-*` toolbox could grow into (per operator's original prompt):

- `/az-review <subscription|rg|resource>` — CAF/WAF env-audit (DISCOVERY-cluster)
- `/az-meeting-prep <service> <customer-context>` — meeting-specific prep ovanpå TLDR
- `/az-build-alz` — generate ALZ from context
- `/az-build-slz` — sovereign-LZ variant
- `/az-bicep-from-context <user-need>` — Bicep generation
- `/az-cost-estimate <bicep-or-arm>` — pre-deploy cost forecast
- `/az-pitfalls <service>` — quick fallgropar-snabbcheck (sub-skill, can also be section pulled from TLDR)
- `/az-current-news <area>` — light WebSearch-wrapper for "latest greatest" (would need Premise-4-revisit)

Sequence is operator-controlled per dogfood-feedback.

## Subagent integration mechanics

Per Premise 5, `/az-tldr` will invoke v3 subagents in two modes:

**Mode 1 (deterministic):** Service's `agent-mapping.yaml` specifies which agents own which sections. SKILL.md spawns them explicitly with context.

**Mode 2 (advisory):** Operator can invoke with `--with-agent <AgentName>` flag to override or add. E.g. `/az-tldr expressroute --with-agent BicepReviewer` if a customer-IaC discussion is upcoming.

Agents invoked via Claude Code's Task tool (or equivalent in other CLIs).

## Distribution Plan

- v3.5 ships på samma `v3-dev` branch som v3.0.0 (extends, doesn't fork).
- Operator dogfoodar via `claude --plugin-dir E:/Workspace/jokerman-session-setup` (no plugin re-install needed).
- After dogfooding cycle (1-2 weeks), if validation green:
  - PR `v3-dev → main`
  - Tag `v3.0.0` (includes v3.5 Azure toolbox seed)
  - Submit to Anthropic marketplace (per existing v3 ship-gate plan)
- v3.5 is positioned in CHANGELOG.md as "v3.5 Azure toolbox seed: first /az-* weapon."

## Dependencies

- v3-dev branch (current) — already shipped this session
- `/generate-web` skill — present in v3 (for `--html` flag)
- 15 ms-specific agents — present in v3
- Voice corpus calibration — NOT required for v3.5 (toolbox is `voice: internal`)
- MS brand assets at `~/.jstack/brand/` — optional (default fallback template works)

## Open Questions

1. **Section selection in `--brief` mode.** Should operator be able to ask `/az-tldr expressroute --brief` for a 100-word TLDR vs `--full` for the entire 15-section rundown? (Probably yes — common UX expectation. Add to v3.5 if simple, defer to v3.6 otherwise.)
2. **Service-content authorship.** Operator writes ExpressRoute content for v3.5 alone. For v3.6+ services, do we want a `/skillify-az` skill that scaffolds new service files via guided questions? (Likely yes — operator-burden compounds otherwise.)
3. **Section-level caching.** Subagent calls per section are expensive. Cache per (service, section, agent, date) to avoid re-spawning agents in repeated invocations? (Recommend NO for v3.5 — premature optimization. Re-evaluate post-dogfood if cost is felt.)
4. **Cross-CLI agent invocation.** Claude Code has Task tool; Codex uses `codex exec` subprocess; Cursor uses Background Agents. How does `/az-tldr` invoke subagents in non-Claude CLIs? (Per v3 portability stance — degraded in non-Claude. Document as such; full agent-orchestration is Claude-Code-native in v3.5.)
5. **Quarterly refresh tracking.** When ExpressRoute content's `as_of` date is >90 days old, should a hook warn? (Recommend YES — reuse `brand-staleness-warn` hook pattern, create new `az-content-stale-warn` hook in v3.5.)

## Success Criteria

**Operator-validation triggers (measurable within 2 weeks of ship):**
1. Operator invokes `/az-tldr expressroute` at least 3 times for real Azure prep
2. Operator's prep-time drops from 60-120 min to <30 min för en ExpressRoute-prep session
3. Operator notes ≥1 section that was "exactly what was needed" — section-level fitness
4. Operator notes ≥1 friction-point in the workflow (UX gap) — basis för v3.6 iteration
5. Operator considers ExpressRoute content's depth/freshness "good enough to share with a CAIP-SE colleague" (proxy for team-adoption potential)

**Negative signals (would trigger redesign):**
- Operator stops invoking after first try (= shape is wrong)
- Operator finds curated content shallower than 30 min of Learn-stitching (= content-bar too low)
- Subagent output adds noise instead of value (= agent-orchestration is wrong for KNOWLEDGE-cluster)

## The Assignment

**Operator's concrete real-world action after this design is approved:**

> Before next ExpressRoute-relevant customer conversation, even if v3.5 isn't shipped yet, manually go through your usual ExpressRoute-prep flow and take SCREENSHOTS or note timestamps for: (a) where you start, (b) which tabs you open in what order, (c) where you got stuck or repeated searches, (d) what you wished was already in front of you. This becomes evidence-grounded scaffolding for `services/expressroute.md` — instead of writing curated content from memory, you'll write from a real prep-session-painmap. Take the screenshots before you implement, so the implementation is grounded in workflow truth.

## What I noticed about how you think

- **Du korrigerade mig på D4 utan att tveka.** Jag tryckte "lean MVP, 1 skill, 1 service." Du svarade: "Kom ihåg det här är olika cmds/skills, tldr azure är en on demand tool, az-review är nästa vapen i lådan, vi har behov av massa sånt här." Det var inte ett "ja men" — det var en arkitekturell rättning. Du tänker i toolbox-mönster, inte i feature-pipeline. Det är skillnaden mellan platform-thinking och product-thinking.

- **Du valde B över min A-rekommendation.** Jag rekommenderade lean MVP (A) för speed-to-validation. Du valde agent-integrated (B) — och resonemanget var inte "B är coolare", det var "v3 har 78 agents, de måste börja arbeta." Du investerar i att din tidigare investering ger avkastning, inte att den blir bortglömd. Det är ovanligt — många operator-builders glömmer förra månadens kod.

- **Du sa "tänk alltid på fallgropar" och "tänk dig pinsamheten."** Två gånger i prompten. Inte "tänk på kvalitet" eller "tänk på excellens" — pinsamhet. Den specifika rädslan att stå framför kund och inte veta något du borde veta. Det är CAIP-SE-rollens kärnstress, och du namnger den direkt. Verktyget ska skydda mot pinsamhet. Den framing styr designen.

- **Du skrev hela visionen från första meddelandet.** 15+ sektioner, 4 use-cases, 10+ services i sikte. Du har redan tänkt på detta — office-hours-jobbet är inte att brainstorma, det är att hitta vilken bit som ska shippas först. När någon redan vet vad de vill måste forcing-frågorna vara om SCOPE och PRIORITERING, inte IDÉ. Det fungerade här.
